title: arXiv Trending Mathematics — Week of 2026-09-18 to 2026-09-25

sections.title: Localization near the edge for the lattice Anderson-Bernoulli model on general dimension
sections.abstract: The authors prove Anderson localization near the bottom of the spectrum for the lattice Anderson model with Bernoulli potential in every dimension d ≥ 2, completing a problem left open by Bourgain and Kenig.
sections.claimed_result: The paper establishes spectral and strong dynamical localization near the spectral bottom, with pure point spectrum and exponentially decaying eigenfunctions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The operator is the discrete Anderson model on ℓ²(Z^d) with i.i.d. Bernoulli potential; the main theorem gives an energy interval depending on dimension and disorder.
sections.caveat: This is an attributed preprint claim and is a near-edge, not full-spectrum, localization theorem.

sections.title: Global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical NLS
sections.abstract: The authors prove global well-posedness and scattering for the three-dimensional focusing energy-critical nonlinear Schrödinger equation below both the ground-state energy and gradient thresholds.
sections.claimed_result: Every datum in homogeneous H¹(R³) below both sharp thresholds generates a global solution scattering in both time directions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The equation is focusing energy-critical cubic NLS on R³; both strict threshold inequalities are required and finite mass is not assumed.
sections.caveat: The result is a preprint theorem and does not cover data at or above the sharp thresholds.

sections.title: Bounded-orbit wandering domains do not exist
sections.abstract: The paper proves that transcendental entire functions have no wandering Fatou components with bounded forward orbit, and proves the stronger analogous statement for transcendental meromorphic functions.
sections.claimed_result: Wandering Fatou components have unbounded forward union, and every point in a meromorphic wandering domain has an unbounded orbit along a subsequence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The maps are transcendental entire or meromorphic functions and the domains are pairwise-distinct wandering Fatou components.
sections.caveat: The result is specific to holomorphic dynamics and does not extend to general quasiregular maps.

sections.title: Sharp Lovász-Theta Bounds on Random Graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove that the Lovász theta function of G(n,1/2) is (1+o(1))√n with high probability.
sections.claimed_result: The paper closes the previous factor-of-two asymptotic gap for the Lovász theta number of an Erdős–Rényi random graph.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The graph is G(n,1/2) and the conclusion is asymptotic and high-probability.
sections.caveat: Extensions to other graph distributions require separate arguments.

sections.title: Thresholds and spread in set systems of bounded VC-dimension
sections.abstract: For bounded-VC-dimension set systems, the paper proves a logarithmic threshold comparison, verifies Talagrand's integral–fractional conjecture in fixed VC-dimension, and improves sunflower bounds.
sections.claimed_result: It proves p_c(F) ≤ C q(F) log(d+1) and derives robust and ordinary sunflower consequences.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: F is a family of nonempty subsets of a finite set with VC-dimension at most d.
sections.caveat: The logarithmic factor is claimed optimal only up to absolute constants.

sections.title: A 1/64 spectral gap for surfaces with δ=1/2
sections.abstract: For a range of convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces, the authors prove an explicit essential spectral gap and obtain a 1/64−ε gap at δ=1/2.
sections.claimed_result: The essential spectral gap has size β = 7/8(1/2−δ)+δ/32−ε in the stated δ-range.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The surfaces are convex co-compact hyperbolic surfaces and δ is the Poincaré-series exponent.
sections.caveat: The theorem has a restricted δ-range and includes an arbitrary ε>0.

sections.title: A quasisymmetric analog of Grassmannian Schubert varieties
sections.abstract: The paper relates toric Richardson cohomology and homology to quasisymmetric and noncommutative symmetric functions and derives log-concavity consequences.
sections.claimed_result: Toric Richardson cohomology rings are finite truncations of quasisymmetric functions, with a direct-limit structure and a shard-polytope log-concavity consequence.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The objects are toric Richardson varieties in Grassmannians and their direct limit.
sections.caveat: The proposed identification with a Baker–Richter-type H-group remains conjectural.

sections.title: On the largest common subtree of uniform attachment trees
sections.abstract: For two independent n-vertex uniform attachment trees, the paper proves that their largest common subtree has at least n^0.83 vertices with high probability.
sections.claimed_result: The common subtree lower bound is n^0.83 with high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The trees are unlabeled uniform attachment trees, also called random recursive trees.
sections.caveat: The true order of the largest common subtree remains open and the exponent may not be sharp.
